seo.title: A panel for any plugin | OpenMixer
seo.description: How omx-panel gives an LV2 or CLAP plugin a panel without drawing one: a MOD GUI, controller pages and a host layout, from what the plugin declares.

hero.title: A panel for any plugin, without drawing one.
hero.lede: omx-panel reads what a plugin declares about itself and produces its panel: the controls, their ranges and their grouping. Nobody draws it by hand.

pitch.title: What you get.
pitch.what: Give any LV2 or CLAP plugin a panel, from the plugin's own declaration:
pitch.modgui: a MOD GUI, the format MOD and Zynthian draw;
pitch.controller: pages for a controller, eight controls to a page;
pitch.host: a layout for a host that draws its own panel.
pitch.look: Every panel wears the omx look, vintage or modern.

steps.title: The three steps.

declare.title: The plugin declares itself.
declare.text: A plugin states its controls: symbol, travel, default, label and group. That statement, the descriptor, is the only input. A descriptor comes from scanning the plugin, or from a package that installs it, such as omx-plugins. The panel never holds a range of its own.

layout.title: omx-panel lays it out.
layout.text: It orders the controls into sections, gives each a role, picks the family the controls make together and cuts the pages of eight a controller shows. When the plugin declares a panel of its own, that panel wins.

write.title: omx-panel writes the panel.
write.text: For MOD and Zynthian it writes a MOD GUI into the plugin's LV2 bundle: modgui.ttl and a modgui/ directory. A toggle becomes a switch, a choice or a short integer travel a selector, and every other travel a knob.

steps.commands: The command takes a descriptor file and the bundle to write into:
steps.check: The second line writes nothing: it compares the bundle with what the descriptor would produce and refuses a stale, missing or extra file.

author.title: For a plugin author.
author.skin: A plugin that wants its own drawing ships a skin package: a directory named after the plugin, holding a skin.json that says how the panel is drawn and the licence of everything in it. Ranges, units and scales stay in the plugin's description; the skin refers to controls by id. Check a package before you install it:
author.import: A plugin that already ships a MOD GUI does not start from nothing: omx-panel import reads the bundle and the plugin's licence and writes a skin package from them. A bundle whose licence is missing or not on the allow-list is refused with a named code, and nothing is written.
